diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $A_H \in \mathcal{M}\left(\lambda^{\prime}, \Lambda^{\prime} ; D_T\right)$, and we define $b_H^{\varepsilon}=\rho a^{\varepsilon}+(1-\rho) A_H$.

issues.failure_explanation: No ellipticity, boundedness, or sufficiently small-error condition is imposed on the main-scheme coefficient $A_H$. Consequently $b_H^\varepsilon$ need not be coercive, so the linear problems defining $U_k$ and $U_0$ need not be uniquely solvable, while all subsequent stability and projection arguments use coercivity with constant $\lambda$.

failure_location.quote: In practice, the hybrid coefficient $b_H^\varepsilon(x)=\rho(x) a^\varepsilon(x)+(1-\rho(x))A_H(x)$, where $A_H$ is the approximation of $A$ obtained by HMM or other types of numerical homogenization methods.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require $A_H$ to belong uniformly to an ellipticity class with constants independent of the discretization parameters, or impose a quantitative error condition guaranteeing that property, and update constants accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Well-posedness of the numerical method and every error or stability result involving $b_H^\varepsilon$ are unsupported for the stated class of numerical homogenization outputs.
issues.title: The discrete scheme does not assume that the numerical effective coefficient is elliptic
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis restores coercivity without changing the method, rates, or principal guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The source term $f\in L^2(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ and initial value $u_0\in H_0^1(D)$.

issues.failure_explanation: An $L^2$-in-time source has no well-defined values $f(t_k)$. Likewise the weak parabolic regularity stated for $u^\varepsilon$ gives $\partial_tu^\varepsilon$ only as an $L^2$-in-time $H^{-1}$ equivalence class, so the nodal quantities $\partial_tu_k^\varepsilon$ used in the local proofs and discrete norms are undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use time-cell averages of $f$ and of the weak time derivative, rewriting the discrete consistency identities accordingly, or add temporal regularity that supplies canonical point values.
issues.overall_effect: The scheme is not defined on the paper's stated source space, and the microscopic error terms and pointwise-in-time PDE identities used in the local theorems are not meaningful under their hypotheses.
issues.title: The method and local estimates sample time-equivalence classes at grid points
issues.why_classification: Time averaging is a standard local modification and can preserve the backward-Euler method and its stated rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the transition function $\rho=\chi_K$; i.e. the indicative function of $K$, then the H-limit of the concurrent coefficient $b^\varepsilon$ is exactly the effective matrix $A$.

issues.failure_explanation: Only bounded measurability of $\rho$ is stated, but the proof differentiates $(1-\rho)\varphi\phi^\varepsilon$ in both space and time and uses it as an admissible parabolic test function. These operations are unjustified for a general bounded transition and are especially invalid for the indicator functions explicitly included in the claimed scope. The asserted weighted energy-limit identities therefore do not follow from the displayed argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a valid localization or approximation argument for bounded measurable transitions, including passage to indicators, or restrict the proposition to sufficiently regular $\rho$ and prove the indicator assertion separately.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise estimate for the H-limit and its $A_H$ extension are unproved for the advertised nonsmooth transition functions, including the indicator case emphasized later.
issues.title: The H-convergence proof tests with an inadmissibly rough transition function
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a nontrivial H-convergence localization argument or a meaningful restriction of scope, but it is confined to this coefficient-limit analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: The projection estimate proved and used in the argument requires approximation over all of $K$, whereas the theorem's right-hand side contains only the strictly smaller $K_0$ norm. An infimum measured on $K_0$ cannot control the approximation and transition errors on $K\setminus K_0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the approximation norm over $K_0$ by the norm over $K$ throughout the theorem statement, matching the estimate actually derived.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By $\int_K (u^\varepsilon_k-\chi_k) \mathrm{d}x=0$ and Poincaré inequality on $K$, we have

issues.failure_explanation: The proof selects an unconstrained minimizer of a gradient seminorm and then imposes a prescribed mean on it. Since global constants generally do not belong to $X_{h,H}\subset H_0^1(D)$, an unconstrained minimizer cannot in general be shifted to obtain that mean while remaining in the finite element space. Replacing it by a mean-constrained minimizer would not justify the final comparison with the unconstrained infimum. Thus the Poincaré step essential to the claimed best-approximation bound lacks a valid construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct a finite-element mean correction and prove its approximation cost, or weaken the theorem to a mean-constrained best-approximation term, with appropriate connectedness or componentwise conditions on $K$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the indicator-transition local estimate does not establish its leading unconstrained best-approximation term.
issues.title: The best approximant in the indicator-case proof cannot be assigned the required mean
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial approximation construction or a substantive weakening of the leading term is required; the remaining local-estimate architecture can be retained.
